requirements.title: Perimeter
requirements.text: The site boundary deters, detects, and delays unauthorized entry by people and vehicles.

citation.source: UFC 4-022-03, Security Fencing and Gates, US Department of Defense
citation.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

requirements.title: Boundary defined and marked
requirements.text: The site boundary is physically delineated and posted so that unauthorized entry is clearly identifiable.

citation.source: ASIS PAP.1-2012, Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection

requirements.title: Barrier height and condition
requirements.text: Perimeter barriers meet the site's specified height and are free of breaches, ground gaps, and damage.

citation.source: UFC 4-022-03, Security Fencing and Gates, US Department of Defense
citation.section: Fence fabric, height, and ground clearance
citation.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

requirements.title: Clear zones maintained
requirements.text: Clear zones on both sides of perimeter barriers are kept free of climb aids, vegetation, and objects that provide concealment.

citation.source: UFC 4-022-03, Security Fencing and Gates, US Department of Defense
citation.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

requirements.title: Gates and openings controlled
requirements.text: Gates, culverts, and other openings in the perimeter are secured or controlled to the same level as the barrier.

citation.source: UFC 4-022-03, Security Fencing and Gates, US Department of Defense
citation.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

requirements.title: Vehicle approach controlled
requirements.text: Vehicle approaches to occupied buildings and critical assets are controlled with barriers and standoff distance matched to the threat.

citation.source: UFC 4-020-01, DoD Security Engineering Facilities Planning Manual
citation.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

requirements.title: Access control
requirements.text: Entry to the site, buildings, and restricted areas is limited to authorized people.

citation.source: ASIS PAP.1-2012, Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection

requirements.title: Entry points controlled
requirements.text: Every exterior door and every door into a restricted area is controlled by an electronic or mechanical access control or by staff.

citation.source: ASIS PAP.1-2012, Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection

requirements.title: Credential lifecycle managed
requirements.text: Credentials are issued on authorization, reviewed periodically, and revoked promptly when no longer needed.

citation.source: ASIS PAP.1-2012, Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection

requirements.title: Visitors managed
requirements.text: Visitors are identified, recorded, badged, and escorted where required.

citation.source: ASIS PAP.1-2012, Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection

requirements.title: Door status monitored
requirements.text: Controlled doors report forced and held-open conditions to a staffed monitoring point.

citation.source: CISA physical security guidance (Physical Security resources, cisa.gov)
citation.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

requirements.title: Restricted areas segregated
requirements.text: Restricted areas such as server rooms, cash rooms, and loading docks have separate access rights limited to named people.

citation.source: ASIS PAP.1-2012, Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection

requirements.title: Tailgating countered
requirements.text: Main controlled entries have measures that prevent or detect more than one person entering on a single authorization.

citation.source: CISA physical security guidance (Physical Security resources, cisa.gov)
citation.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

requirements.title: Video surveillance and camera positioning
requirements.text: Cameras are positioned and configured so that recorded video can detect, observe, recognize, or identify as the purpose requires.

citation.source: IEC 62676-4, Video surveillance systems for use in security applications, Part 4: Application guidelines

requirements.title: Coverage of entries and critical areas
requirements.text: Entrances, perimeter lines, parking, and critical assets are within camera fields of view with no unplanned blind spots.

citation.source: IEC 62676-4, Video surveillance systems for use in security applications, Part 4: Application guidelines

requirements.title: Pixel density matched to purpose
requirements.text: Each camera delivers the pixel density on target needed for its purpose (detect, observe, recognize, identify) in day and night conditions.

citation.source: IEC 62676-4, Video surveillance systems for use in security applications, Part 4: Application guidelines
citation.section: DORI pixel density table (about 25, 62, 125, and 250 pixels per meter)

requirements.title: Recording and retention
requirements.text: Video is recorded and retained for the period set by policy or regulation, with accurate time stamps and a controlled export process.

citation.source: IEC 62676-4, Video surveillance systems for use in security applications, Part 4: Application guidelines

requirements.title: System health and cybersecurity
requirements.text: Cameras and recorders are monitored for failure and hardened (no default passwords, segmented network, current firmware).

citation.source: CISA physical security guidance (Physical Security resources, cisa.gov)
citation.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

requirements.title: Intruder alarms
requirements.text: Intrusion detection covers likely entry routes and alarms reach a responder who acts.

citation.source: NFPA 731, Standard for the Installation of Electronic Premises Security Systems

requirements.title: Detection coverage
requirements.text: Exterior openings and high-value interior areas are covered by intrusion sensors.

citation.source: NFPA 731, Standard for the Installation of Electronic Premises Security Systems

requirements.title: Monitoring and response
requirements.text: Alarms are monitored around the clock by a certified central station or a staffed console, with a documented response.

citation.source: UL 2050, Standard for National Industrial Security Systems; UL certificate programs for alarm monitoring

requirements.title: Testing and maintenance
requirements.text: The system is tested end to end on a defined schedule and faults are corrected.

citation.source: NFPA 731, Standard for the Installation of Electronic Premises Security Systems

requirements.title: Duress and panic
requirements.text: Duress or panic alarms are provided where staff face threats, and are tested.

citation.source: NFPA 731, Standard for the Installation of Electronic Premises Security Systems

requirements.title: Locks and hardware
requirements.text: Doors, frames, windows, and locks resist forced and covert entry, and keys are controlled.

citation.source: ANSI/BHMA A156 series, Builders Hardware standards (for example A156.2 bored locks, A156.13 mortise locks)

requirements.title: Hardware grade and condition
requirements.text: Locks and door hardware on exterior and restricted doors are commercial grade and in working order.

citation.source: ANSI/BHMA A156 series, Builders Hardware standards (for example A156.2 bored locks, A156.13 mortise locks)

requirements.title: Key and combination control
requirements.text: Keys and combinations are registered, issued on authorization, recovered, and changed when compromised.

citation.source: ASIS PAP.1-2012, Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection

requirements.title: Door, frame, and window hardening
requirements.text: Hinges, latches, frames, and accessible windows resist removal, shimming, and prying.

citation.source: UFC 4-020-01, DoD Security Engineering Facilities Planning Manual
citation.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

requirements.title: Lighting
requirements.text: Security lighting lets people and cameras see at night without glare or dark gaps.

citation.source: ANSI/IES G-1, Guide for Security Lighting for People, Property, and Critical Infrastructure

requirements.title: Illuminance levels
requirements.text: Measured illuminance at parking, paths, and entrances meets the site's design target (for example from IES RP-20 or IES G-1).

citation.source: ANSI/IES RP-20, Lighting for Parking Facilities

requirements.title: Uniformity and continuity
requirements.text: Lighting is uniform enough to avoid dark gaps along routes and across parking areas.

citation.source: ANSI/IES RP-20, Lighting for Parking Facilities

requirements.title: Controls, maintenance, and power
requirements.text: Lights are automatically controlled, outages are repaired promptly, and critical lighting has backup power.

citation.source: ANSI/IES G-1, Guide for Security Lighting for People, Property, and Critical Infrastructure

requirements.title: Coordination with cameras and sightlines
requirements.text: Fixtures do not shine into camera lenses or guard sightlines.

citation.source: ANSI/IES G-1, Guide for Security Lighting for People, Property, and Critical Infrastructure

requirements.title: Guard operations
requirements.text: Security officers are directed, trained, equipped, and supervised for the duties of each post.

citation.source: ASIS PAP.1-2012, Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection

requirements.title: Post orders
requirements.text: Each post has current written post orders that officers have read.

citation.source: ASIS PAP.1-2012, Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection

requirements.title: Patrol verification
requirements.text: Patrols are scheduled and their completion is verified.

citation.source: ASIS PAP.1-2012, Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection

requirements.title: Training and licensing
requirements.text: Officers hold required licenses and documented site training.

citation.source: ASIS PAP.1-2012, Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection

requirements.title: Communications and reporting
requirements.text: Officers can reach supervisors and responders at all times and record incidents in a reviewed log.

citation.source: ASIS PAP.1-2012, Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection

requirements.title: Staffing
requirements.text: Required posts are staffed for their scheduled hours.

citation.source: ASIS PAP.1-2012, Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection

requirements.title: Policies and procedures
requirements.text: Physical security is governed by documented, approved, and exercised policies and procedures.

citation.source: ASIS PAP.1-2012, Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection

requirements.title: Physical security policy
requirements.text: A written physical security policy is approved by management and reviewed on a schedule.

citation.source: ASIS PAP.1-2012, Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection

requirements.title: Security risk assessment
requirements.text: A documented security risk assessment for the site is current.

citation.source: ASIS PAP.1-2012, Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection

requirements.title: Emergency plans and drills
requirements.text: Emergency action plans, including lockdown and evacuation, are documented and exercised.

citation.source: CISA physical security guidance (Physical Security resources, cisa.gov)
citation.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

requirements.title: Personnel security and awareness
requirements.text: Staff with unescorted access are screened, and staff receive security awareness training.

citation.source: ASIS PAP.1-2012, Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection

requirements.title: Information and media handling
requirements.text: Sensitive documents and media are protected, critical areas are not advertised, and disposal is controlled.

citation.source: ASIS PAP.1-2012, Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection
